oracle.explanation: The oracle builds a minimal, dependency-free DOM shim (Document/Element/Text/DocumentFragment) exposing exactly the surface DOMPurify needs (createElement, createElementNS, createTextNode, createDocumentFragment, document.implementation.createHTMLDocument, Node traversal/mutation methods, and a tiny tag-soup innerHTML parser/serializer). This avoids requiring jsdom or any other dependency while still letting DOMPurify's real sanitize() logic run against a genuine DOM-like tree built from parsed markup. First, a benign sanitize() call on a simple '...' string is used to prove the pipeline (shim + DOMPurify initialization + parsing + serialization) works end-to-end; only if that succeeds is operation_completed set true. Then a known nested template/select/style mutation-XSS payload (the class of mXSS bypass fixed after 3.2.3) is sanitized. If the resulting output still contains the event-handler attribute carrying the unique marker, the exploit is considered successful; in the patched version the stricter mutation handling removes the handler, so the marker/handler combination disappears from the output, yielding exploit_succeeded=false while operation_completed remains true because the benign call already succeeded.
